meta.caveat: Architecture-first seed for UI; not claimed ladder-optimal. Scores describe species/form tendencies across plausible Champions doubles architectures rather than one exact set.
meta.scale: All numeric scores are integers 0–5 unless noted. 0 = absent, 3 = solid, 5 = elite for Champions doubles architectures.

metricDefs.label: Engine Participation Count
metricDefs.meaning: How many distinct win engines / infrastructure loops this species can meaningfully participate in across common Champions doubles architectures, rather than within only one team.

metricDefs.label: Engine Exclusivity Tax
metricDefs.meaning: How often teammates must become dedicated servants for this species to function. High tax means packages collapse around it; low tax means many packages can support it lightly.

metricDefs.label: Bridge Quality
metricDefs.meaning: How effectively this species participates in separate modules without forcing either module to compromise.

metricDefs.label: Create Fan-Out
metricDefs.meaning: How many strategically distinct teammate roles can consume what this species creates.

metricDefs.label: Convert Fan-Out
metricDefs.meaning: How many distinct infrastructure forms this species can convert into progress, such as weather, Tailwind, Fake Out turns, terrain, Intimidate turns, screens, Trick Room, redirection, or free setup turns.

metricDefs.label: MAG
metricDefs.meaning: Marginal Architecture Gain — how much genuinely new strategic territory this species tends to open on Champions doubles sixes at species baseline rather than in one specific six.

metricDefs.label: Module Elasticity Support
metricDefs.meaning: As a root or key module, how many strategically different packages it can support without rebuilding the six.

metricDefs.label: Engine-Converter Continuity
metricDefs.meaning: How effectively this species can create a favorable resource or state and later personally convert that same state into damage, control, scaling, or a win condition instead of requiring another dedicated converter.

teamContextRules.cMagHint: Start with species-baseline MAG, then inspect the five teammates for duplicated territory. Raise C-MAG when the candidate adds a genuinely new engine, failure condition, speed state, damage axis, counterplay inversion, Mega package, or conversion route that existing teammates can also exploit. Lower C-MAG when it merely strengthens an already-saturated route without creating a meaningfully different package or failure state.
teamContextRules.exclusivityGivenSix: Lower Engine Exclusivity Tax when the other five already provide the infrastructure this species wants while remaining useful in unrelated packages. Lower it further when the species can function autonomously after consuming that infrastructure. Raise it when several teammates must change moves, items, Mega choice, positioning, speed profiles, or normal roles primarily to enable this species. Shared infrastructure with multiple consumers lowers tax; dedicated servants raise it.
teamContextRules.saturation: Adding another member of the same archetype lowers C-MAG when both create or consume the same resources, compete for the same setup or Mega turn, fail to the same counterplay, or improve the same packages without opening new ones. Functional redundancy remains valuable when the new species converts shared infrastructure differently, creates another speed or damage state, supplies a different endgame, or turns the first route's counterplay into progress for a second route.

profiles.name: Abomasnow
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Abomasnow is more architecturally valuable than a slow Ice attacker because one slot both creates Snow and immediately spends it.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High ECC with better Fan-Out when several teammates exploit Snow rather than only Abomasnow.
antiPatterns: Building a full Snow package around only one Blizzard user

profiles.name: Mega Abomasnow
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Often judged as a slow Ice attacker, but its stronger architectural feature is one-slot weather creation plus immediate self-conversion.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Excellent ECC: it creates Snow and can personally spend the weather immediately.
antiPatterns: Adding several dedicated Snow servants when only Abomasnow meaningfully converts Snow
profiles.caveat: Exact M-C set quality is matchup-dependent; score emphasizes weather compression rather than usage.

profiles.name: Absol
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Its create-web is modest; most architectural value comes from lightly supported conversion.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Good generic Fan-In without requiring a dedicated package.
antiPatterns: Spending several support slots to force Absol attacks

profiles.name: Mega Absol
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Its outward create-web is modest, but it is easier to support lightly than many dedicated Mega sweepers.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Good Fan-In from generic tempo resources, but less self-contained than top conversion Megas.
antiPatterns: Treating Magic Bounce-style utility as enough reason to consume the Mega slot
profiles.caveat: Architectural score is more confident than any claim about current tournament prevalence.

profiles.name: Mega Absol Z
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Connector metrics underrate it because most arrows point inward; its value is how many generic tempo resources it can turn into immediate progress.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High convert Fan-Out and relatively low servant tax make it a stronger architecture candidate than a thin create-web suggests.
antiPatterns: Building four support slots solely to manufacture Absol attack turns
profiles.caveat: New M-C Mega; role breadth should be updated as tournament sets stabilize.

profiles.name: Aegislash
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Aegislash's value is state elasticity: the same slot can alternate defensive resource creation and offensive conversion.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Elite ECC because defensive stance manipulation manufactures the turns that Blade form later spends.
antiPatterns: Playing Aegislash as a static attacker instead of exploiting stance transitions

profiles.name: Aerodactyl
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Aerodactyl is valuable because speed control, disruption, Rock pressure, and Ground immunity coexist without demanding a dedicated shell.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Solid ECC: it can create Tailwind and personally use the resulting speed state.
antiPatterns: Using Aerodactyl only as a disposable Tailwind button

profiles.name: Mega Aerodactyl
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Its best architectural feature is low exclusivity: speed control, disruption, and offense can coexist without demanding a dedicated team.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Not the strongest raw converter, but unusually easy to insert into unrelated packages.
antiPatterns: Using the Mega slot only for marginally stronger Rock damage

profiles.name: Aggron
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Aggron's bulk is meaningful, but it needs shared slow-game infrastructure to turn that bulk into tournament-grade progress.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Moderate Fan-In with higher speed-state tax than premium converters.
antiPatterns: Creating Trick Room solely to rescue Aggron's speed

profiles.name: Mega Aggron
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Its raw defensive value is real, but it often needs the rest of the six to slow the game enough for that value to convert.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Can consume several defensive infrastructures but rarely creates the speed or tempo state itself.
antiPatterns: Adding too many passive partners and producing a team that cannot convert durability into KOs

profiles.name: Alakazam
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: A thin outward graph should not hide its elite conversion surface area.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Very high Fan-In with little servant tax because natural speed reduces support requirements.
antiPatterns: Confusing low create Fan-Out with low architectural value

profiles.name: Mega Alakazam
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: A classic example of a thin outward graph masking elite conversion Fan-In.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Many generic infrastructures support it without becoming servants, but Alakazam itself creates relatively little durable infrastructure.
antiPatterns: Confusing high speed and damage with high bridge value

profiles.name: Alcremie
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Alcremie is strongest when its amplification can feed multiple unrelated damage clocks rather than one designated carry.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Low personal conversion, but excellent outward Fan-Out keeps exclusivity low.
antiPatterns: Using amplification support for only one teammate

profiles.name: Altaria
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Altaria's architecture comes from fitting several positional and speed-control jobs into one low-tax slot.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Solid Fan-In without needing dedicated servants.
antiPatterns: Giving Altaria too many utility jobs and no conversion route

profiles.name: Mega Altaria
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Role flexibility helps it bridge packages, though it rarely creates a single overwhelming infrastructure state.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Can spend many generic balance resources and remain useful without dedicated servants.
antiPatterns: Giving it too many utility jobs and losing an actual conversion route

profiles.name: Ampharos
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Ampharos can consume common slow-game infrastructure but rarely creates enough of its own to anchor a six.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Moderate Fan-In with meaningful Trick Room dependence.
antiPatterns: Building a slow mode that only Ampharos truly needs

profiles.name: Mega Ampharos
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Strong converter under slow-board infrastructure, but usually does not justify reorganizing multiple partners around it.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Good Fan-In from Trick Room and tempo support; modest outward engine creation.
antiPatterns: Forcing Trick Room solely because Ampharos is slow

profiles.name: Annihilape
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: One of the strongest inward-conversion profiles because normal opponent counterplay can become its resource.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Excellent convert Fan-Out with minimal servant tax; can play immediate or scaling identities depending set.
antiPatterns: Assuming every Annihilape must be a slow Rage Fist composition

profiles.name: Appletun
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Appletun becomes useful when its bulk and debuff pressure serve a wider slow-control network instead of one isolated endgame.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Good defensive Fan-In but modest speed-state autonomy.
antiPatterns: Playing for endless sustain without a closing clock

profiles.name: Araquanid
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Araquanid is a strong dual-state consumer because Rain and Trick Room can independently amplify it.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High Fan-In, especially when Rain and Trick Room already serve other teammates.
antiPatterns: Using both Rain and Trick Room solely to enable Araquanid

profiles.name: Arbok
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Arbok's value is primarily low-cost physical control rather than personal conversion ceiling.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Moderate ECC through Intimidate-enabled disruption.
antiPatterns: Using Arbok without teammates that can spend Intimidate-created safety

profiles.name: Arboliva
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Arboliva's terrain creation can support several packages, but activation timing is less controllable than Rillaboom's.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Good ECC once Terrain is active; reasonable slow-game Fan-In.
antiPatterns: Assuming Seed activation timing will always align with the intended turn

profiles.name: Arcanine
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Arcanine is a classic low-tax bridge because Intimidate, Fire pressure, and priority all remain useful in unrelated packages.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Good ECC through Intimidate-created attack windows and Sun conversion.
antiPatterns: Using Intimidate without a plan to convert the reduced-pressure turn

profiles.name: Hisuian Arcanine

converts.into: safe Flare Blitz or Head Smash

profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Hisuian Arcanine is an elite immediate converter because almost any generic tempo resource becomes meaningful damage without setup.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High Fan-In and virtually no servant tax; one of the cleanest instant-conversion nodes.
antiPatterns: Adding elaborate setup support to a Pokémon whose main virtue is immediate conversion

profiles.name: Archaludon
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Rain is the obvious engine, but Stamina lets Archaludon convert opponent attacks even outside dedicated weather.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High Fan-In from Rain, screens, tempo, and opponent contact makes it less weather-exclusive than it first appears.
antiPatterns: Treating Archaludon as unusable whenever Rain is not active

profiles.name: Ariados
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Ariados is primarily an outward control piece; the challenge is whether its support package is efficient enough compared with stronger connectors.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Low personal conversion ceiling.
antiPatterns: Using disruption that does not create a concrete partner advantage

profiles.name: Armarouge
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Armarouge is one of the best shared-infrastructure species because it can set Trick Room and then personally exploit Trick Room, Psychic Terrain, or Sun.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Elite ECC with several independent infrastructure inputs.
antiPatterns: Building hard Trick Room when Armarouge could be one branch of a mixed-speed team

profiles.name: Aromatisse
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Aromatisse's main value is reliable outward Trick Room infrastructure rather than personal conversion.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Low ECC; strongest when several teammates independently consume Trick Room.
antiPatterns: Using Aromatisse when only one teammate wants the slow state

profiles.name: Audino
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Audino has strong outward support but almost no personal conversion, so the rest of the team must provide the clocks.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Low Fan-In by design.
antiPatterns: Building a six that can preserve resources but cannot cash them into progress

profiles.name: Mega Audino
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Outstanding outward support graph but poor ECC; consuming the Mega slot for pure support is a substantial opportunity cost.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Low Fan-In as a personal win condition. Its value is almost entirely what teammates convert.
antiPatterns: Building a passive six where Audino preserves resources but nobody converts them
profiles.caveat: Exact support options should be interpreted set-by-set.

profiles.name: Aurorus
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Aurorus compresses Snow creation and special conversion, but defensive liabilities can raise the practical infrastructure tax.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Good ECC with meaningful slow-board dependence.
antiPatterns: Stacking Snow-only teammates until weather denial collapses the team

profiles.name: Avalugg
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Avalugg can become extremely difficult to remove physically, but several support resources often have to align before that durability becomes a clock.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Moderate Fan-In with high slow-game tax.
antiPatterns: Winning the durability contest without creating offensive progress

profiles.name: Hisuian Avalugg
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Its offensive typing raises conversion potential relative to standard Avalugg, but speed and defensive weaknesses still create infrastructure demands.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Good slow-state converter with moderate exclusivity.
antiPatterns: Building both Snow and Trick Room solely for Hisuian Avalugg

profiles.name: Azumarill
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Azumarill has a high conversion ceiling, but its most explosive setup route can tempt teams into excessive servant support.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High Fan-In with moderate exclusivity; priority helps preserve value after external speed control ends.
antiPatterns: Making every package depend on Belly Drum

profiles.name: Banette
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Banette's main value is action denial that other teammates convert.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Moderate ECC when disruption creates its own later attack windows.
antiPatterns: Using disruption without a partner clock

profiles.name: Mega Banette
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Its create-web can be valuable, but the Mega slot asks whether disruption could be supplied more cheaply elsewhere.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Moderate self-conversion; best when disruption itself directly creates a winning partner turn.
antiPatterns: Using priority utility without a teammate that meaningfully spends the denied action

profiles.name: Barbaracle
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Barbaracle converts many infrastructure forms, but that impressive Fan-In comes with one of the higher exclusivity taxes.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Classic high-Fan-In, high-servant-tax scaler.
antiPatterns: Turning the rest of the team into setup insurance

profiles.name: Mega Barbaracle
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Excellent at consuming generic setup infrastructure, but several teammates often become servants to create the first safe boost.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High Fan-In, high exclusivity tax: a textbook conversion monster that can over-centralize its six.
antiPatterns: Stacking redirection, screens, and Fake Out solely to enable one sweeper
profiles.caveat: Specific optimal Mega Barbaracle loops remain comparatively less tournament-established.

profiles.name: Basculegion Female
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Its endgame clock can convert normal battle attrition into offense, giving it a unique opponent-independent scaling resource.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High Fan-In from Rain, speed, chip, and ally-loss states.
antiPatterns: Sacrificing teammates unnecessarily just to scale Last Respects

profiles.name: Basculegion Male
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Male Basculegion combines Rain conversion, attrition scaling, and priority into a particularly strong endgame profile.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Elite inward conversion with moderate weather dependence.
antiPatterns: Making Rain the only route when Last Respects and priority already create independent clocks

profiles.name: Bastiodon
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Bastiodon can absorb enormous pressure, but converting that survival into a win condition usually requires substantial external help.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Low-to-moderate Fan-In with high exclusivity tax.
antiPatterns: Confusing survival with progress

profiles.name: Baxcalibur
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Does not create much infrastructure, but can convert many common support resources and even some opponent actions.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Strong inward graph with manageable servant tax because it can attack immediately when setup is unavailable.
antiPatterns: Forcing Dragon Dance when immediate Ice or Dragon pressure is already sufficient

profiles.name: Mega Baxcalibur
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: New Mega form should be viewed less as a connector and more as an unusually broad infrastructure consumer.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High conversion surface area with lower support tax than many setup Megas because immediate attacks remain threatening.
antiPatterns: Using every partner to force a boost instead of exploiting immediate pressure
profiles.caveat: New M-C Mega; architecture score should be revisited as more tournament packages establish stable roles.

profiles.name: Beartic
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Beartic can be threatening when weather fixes its speed, but the support cost is high if weather serves nobody else.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Strong weather conversion, weak outward graph.
antiPatterns: Creating weather solely to make Beartic functional

profiles.name: Beedrill
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Beedrill can consume tempo but contributes little infrastructure and is much less autonomous than its Mega form.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Reasonable Fan-In, high fragility tax.
antiPatterns: Using multiple support slots to preserve a low-autonomy attacker

profiles.name: Mega Beedrill
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Very efficient at converting tempo, but fragile and contributes less infrastructure than top bridge Megas.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High speed reduces servant tax; it often needs only light positioning support.
antiPatterns: Spending several team slots compensating for Beedrill's fragility

profiles.name: Bellibolt
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Bellibolt can turn opponent attacks into its own offensive resource, giving it more ECC than a generic slow Electric.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High Fan-In from hits, Trick Room, screens, and tempo.
antiPatterns: Treating Bellibolt as purely passive bulk

profiles.name: Blastoise
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Blastoise is broadly compatible because it can use Rain or generic tempo without demanding either.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Strong Fan-In with low support tax.
antiPatterns: Building Rain solely for Blastoise

profiles.name: Mega Blastoise
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: More autonomous than many bulky Megas because generic speed or Rain support immediately converts into damage.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Broad infrastructure consumer with moderate outward pressure creation.
antiPatterns: Building a full Rain team when Blastoise only needs Rain for select conversion turns

profiles.name: Blaziken
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Blaziken is a premier engine-becomes-converter example because its speed infrastructure is self-generated.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Elite ECC with almost no servant tax.
antiPatterns: Adding redundant speed support when Speed Boost already solves the matchup

profiles.name: Mega Blaziken
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: One of the clearest ECC species: the engine piece and converter are literally the same slot.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Excellent Fan-In with very low exclusivity because Protect or one tempo turn can start the engine.
antiPatterns: Adding redundant external speed control when Speed Boost already solves the relevant tier

profiles.name: Camerupt
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Camerupt is a powerful converter but usually pays a large speed-state tax.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High payoff under shared Trick Room; poor autonomy outside it.
antiPatterns: Creating Trick Room for Camerupt alone

profiles.name: Mega Camerupt
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Enormous conversion payoff, but one of the clearest examples of a high Engine Exclusivity Tax.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Consumes Trick Room exceptionally well, yet often asks the six to supply and preserve that one state.
antiPatterns: Making Trick Room exist primarily for Camerupt rather than several slow converters

profiles.name: Castform
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Castform has unusually broad weather Fan-In but contributes little infrastructure itself.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High conversion breadth, high dependence on external weather.
antiPatterns: Running weather solely so Castform has an identity
profiles.caveat: Architecture value is highly set- and weather-context dependent.

profiles.name: Ceruledge
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Ceruledge forms a closed conversion loop: defensive activation enables setup, setup amplifies Bitter Blade, and damage becomes sustain.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Elite ECC with many generic setup sources and independent Fire/Ghost utility.
antiPatterns: Treating Ceruledge as dependent on one Seed package

profiles.name: Chandelure
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Chandelure can operate across opposite speed states, giving it better module elasticity than many special nukes.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Elite Fan-In from speed control, Sun, and generic tempo.
antiPatterns: Locking Chandelure into only one speed mode

profiles.name: Mega Chandelure
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Unusually flexible for a heavy special Mega because it can participate in both faster and slower speed states.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High conversion surface area; teams need not become dedicated servants if Chandelure is one of several special converters.
antiPatterns: Building exclusively around one speed mode when Chandelure can function in several

profiles.name: Charizard
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Base Charizard's architectural value is unusually tied to Mega Portfolio Value: preview must account for two materially different Mega identities.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Strong Fan-In becomes clearer only when X and Y packages are evaluated separately.
antiPatterns: Treating Charizard as one fixed node rather than a preview fork between Mega identities

profiles.name: Mega Charizard X
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Less outward infrastructure than Charizard Y, but high conversion Fan-In and strong dual-Mega preview value.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Best treated as a physical scaler that can consume many generic free-turn resources.
antiPatterns: Making every support choice serve Dragon Dance

profiles.name: Mega Charizard Y
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: One of the best examples of engine-converter continuity: it creates Sun and immediately becomes one of the strongest Sun converters.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Elite on both axes; teammates can consume its Sun without becoming dedicated servants, while Charizard itself converts several external resources.
antiPatterns: Adding too many Sun-only teammates and making weather denial collapse the entire six
profiles.caveat: Current Champions results have established Mega Charizard Y as a serious Sun architecture root. ([Pokemon][2])

profiles.name: Chesnaught
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Chesnaught is useful when its defensive presence creates turns for a wider balance network.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Moderate Fan-In and moderate autonomy.
antiPatterns: Building too passively around its durability

profiles.name: Mega Chesnaught
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Has more bridge value than a pure wall because its defensive presence can create setup opportunities for partners.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Moderate Fan-In, but teams risk becoming too passive if they overinvest in preserving it.
antiPatterns: Stacking defensive support without a fast route to convert board control

profiles.name: Chimecho
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Chimecho's value is mostly outward infrastructure and sustain rather than personal conversion.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Low ECC; strongest with several shared Trick Room consumers.
antiPatterns: Using Chimecho when only one teammate benefits from its speed state

profiles.name: Mega Chimecho
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Likely stronger as a create-web species than as a personal converter, which makes Mega opportunity cost central to evaluation.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Low-to-moderate personal conversion; strongest when several teammates independently spend its support state.
antiPatterns: Consuming the Mega slot for support when only one teammate benefits
profiles.caveat: Specific M-C package evidence is thinner than for top metagame roots.

profiles.name: Cinderace
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Cinderace has excellent package mobility because broad coverage and speed let it consume generic infrastructure with almost no servant tax.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Elite Fan-In and low exclusivity.
antiPatterns: Over-supporting a naturally autonomous attacker

profiles.name: Clawitzer
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Clawitzer's coverage converts support well, but it does little to create that support state itself.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High inward value with moderate-to-high exclusivity.
antiPatterns: Using multiple support pieces exclusively to compensate for speed

profiles.name: Clefable
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Clefable's broad support web makes it an excellent bridge even when it is not the win condition.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Solid ECC when support transitions into personal scaling.
antiPatterns: Overloading the set with support until Clefable cannot threaten progress

profiles.name: Mega Clefable
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Its best value is role compression: Fairy offense and defensive utility can coexist without demanding a narrow team.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Good Fan-In and solid ECC if configured to transition from support into offense.
antiPatterns: Overloading the set with support and leaving the Mega slot without conversion power

profiles.name: Clodsire
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Clodsire's value is mostly in making certain opponent clocks fail rather than creating fast progress.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Moderate defensive Fan-In; limited offensive conversion.
antiPatterns: Building an entire team around passive denial without a clock

profiles.name: Cofagrigus
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Cofagrigus combines slow-state creation with contact-based ability disruption, giving Trick Room teams a second control axis.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Moderate ECC through contact conversion and room utility.
antiPatterns: Using Trick Room when only one partner wants it

profiles.name: Conkeldurr
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Conkeldurr can convert both friendly slow states and hostile status into offense.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High Fan-In with useful priority reducing speed dependence.
antiPatterns: Treating Trick Room as mandatory when priority can solve the endgame

profiles.name: Corviknight
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: One of the rare non-Megas that can be infrastructure, scaler, and eventual converter without changing slots.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Excellent ECC: creates durable control states and can become the clock itself.
antiPatterns: Running Corviknight as passive Tailwind support when the six needs an independent win condition

profiles.name: Crabominable
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Crabominable can punish the right board brutally, but that board often requires several support concessions.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High slow-state payoff, high exclusivity tax.
antiPatterns: Building hard Trick Room for one converter

profiles.name: Mega Crabominable
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Its damage profile can be excellent, but the architecture often pays heavily to solve its speed and positioning.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Strong Trick Room converter, limited bridge value and relatively high servant tax.
antiPatterns: Building an entire Trick Room shell for one slow attacker

profiles.name: Cyclizar
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Cyclizar is a pure network piece: its main value is transferring position and safety between otherwise unrelated modules.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Personal conversion is moderate, but ECC is good because its own speed powers repeated transitions.
antiPatterns: Using pivot moves without a destination engine worth bringing in

profiles.name: Dachsbun
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Dachsbun gains architecture value when opponent Fire coverage becomes a resource rather than merely something it walls.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Good opponent-funded ECC with low support tax.
antiPatterns: Using Dachsbun when opposing Fire pressure is not structurally relevant

profiles.name: Decidueye
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Decidueye is more useful when trapping or targeting control matters to another engine, not just for its own attacks.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Moderate Fan-In and flexible speed-state use.
antiPatterns: Using trapping without a partner that exploits the immobilized target

profiles.name: Hisuian Decidueye
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Its best architecture comes from combining offense with speed-state manipulation rather than functioning as a standalone breaker.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Good ECC because its attacks can create the speed advantage later actions consume.
antiPatterns: Ignoring speed-control value and using it as only a coverage attacker

profiles.name: Dedenne
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Dedenne is more of a low-cost support bridge than a true conversion monster.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Moderate Fan-In, strong role compression for niche teams.
antiPatterns: Expecting Dedenne to provide both primary support and primary damage

profiles.name: Delphox
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Delphox has unusually broad infrastructure Fan-In across two terrain/weather-style special engines.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High conversion surface area with low servant tax.
antiPatterns: Forcing Sun and Psychic Terrain into one team only for Delphox

profiles.name: Mega Delphox
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: A potentially excellent high-Fan-In Mega because it can spend both Psychic and Fire infrastructures without demanding either.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Strong conversion surface area is more important than its relatively modest create-web.
antiPatterns: Forcing both Sun and Psychic Terrain into the same six solely for Delphox
profiles.caveat: Exact best M-C role remains less established than top-tier Megas.

profiles.name: Diggersby
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Diggersby can participate in opposite speed states and retains priority utility, keeping its support tax low.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High Fan-In with modest outward graph.
antiPatterns: Assuming Diggersby needs setup to function

profiles.name: Ditto
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Ditto's graph is almost entirely inward, but it uniquely converts the opponent's own architecture into its resource.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Elite opponent-funded Fan-In with zero servant tax.
antiPatterns: Bringing Ditto when the opponent has no high-value states worth copying

profiles.name: Dondozo
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Dondozo has enormous MAG but one of the highest exclusivity taxes because Commander architecture consumes roster and bring-four flexibility.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Elite conversion ceiling, poor module independence.
antiPatterns: Mistaking raw Dondozo power for package elasticity

profiles.name: Dragalge
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Dragalge converts slow-game infrastructure well but creates little of it itself.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Good Trick Room Fan-In, moderate tax.
antiPatterns: Creating Trick Room solely for Dragalge

profiles.name: Mega Dragalge
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Useful coverage compression, but slower speed makes its best packages more infrastructure-dependent.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Good Trick Room Fan-In, moderate tax if the six already supports other slow converters.
antiPatterns: Adding Trick Room exclusively to rescue Dragalge's speed

profiles.name: Dragapult
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Dragapult is a premium low-tax bridge because its speed supports offensive, disruptive, and cleanup identities without rebuilding the team.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Elite Fan-In from generic tempo and chip.
antiPatterns: Using Dragapult as a one-dimensional damage slot

profiles.name: Dragonite
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Its strongest quality is package flexibility: support, priority, setup, and Mega ambiguity can coexist across different fours.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High Fan-In with low exclusivity; generic infrastructure usually suffices.
antiPatterns: Assuming Dragonite must be a single fixed physical setup role

profiles.name: Mega Dragonite
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Recent Champions sets show that Mega Dragonite can be infrastructure and attacker rather than merely a bulky Dragon sweeper.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High ECC and excellent Mega Portfolio Value because it can create Tailwind then personally exploit it.
antiPatterns: Treating it only as a late-game cleaner and ignoring its bridge functions
profiles.caveat: Role breadth is supported by contemporary Champions usage, but exact set mix remains team-dependent.

profiles.name: Drampa
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Drampa is a powerful slow-state consumer but offers limited independent engine value.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High Trick Room payoff, high exclusivity.
antiPatterns: Creating a slow mode that only Drampa exploits

profiles.name: Mega Drampa
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Can hit extremely hard under the right state, but the speed-state support often belongs to other teammates rather than Drampa itself.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Strong Trick Room consumer with meaningful exclusivity tax.
antiPatterns: Creating an entire slow mode that only Drampa can exploit

profiles.name: Dudunsparce
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Dudunsparce can mix disruption, durability, and slow offense without requiring one fixed package.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Good ECC through self-created speed and flinch control.
antiPatterns: Running disruption without a closing route

profiles.name: Eelektross
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Eelektross can occupy both slow and mid-speed packages without committing the team to either.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High Fan-In and low support tax.
antiPatterns: Using broad coverage without defining what package problem it solves

profiles.name: Mega Eelektross
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Its unusual defensive and coverage profile can fit both slow and mid-speed modules, giving it better bridge quality than many heavy Megas.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Broad infrastructure consumer that does not necessarily force one dedicated engine.
antiPatterns: Using generic coverage without defining what matchup axis the slot actually adds
profiles.caveat: Specific current tournament role is less established than top M-C Megas.

profiles.name: Emboar
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Emboar converts common slow-game resources well but does not reduce the infrastructure burden itself.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Moderate Fan-In, moderate-to-high exclusivity.
antiPatterns: Making the whole six slow solely for Emboar

profiles.name: Mega Emboar
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Immediate type pressure is useful, but its speed profile often asks the team to provide the state it consumes.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Good slow-board converter, moderate exclusivity.
antiPatterns: Making the whole six slow solely because Emboar prefers Trick Room

profiles.name: Emolga
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Emolga's value is positional: it can redirect Electric pressure and ignore Ground simultaneously.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Moderate opponent-funded ECC.
antiPatterns: Using Emolga when its immunities do not protect high-value partners

profiles.name: Empoleon
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Empoleon has exceptional package flexibility because opponent stat control, Rain, and either speed state can all become resources.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High Fan-In and almost no servant tax.
antiPatterns: Using Empoleon only as a defensive Steel

profiles.name: Espathra
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Espathra's self-generated speed makes it an engine and converter in one slot.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Elite ECC; support tax depends mainly on how much durability its set needs.
antiPatterns: Adding redundant speed control instead of supporting survival or conversion

profiles.name: Espeon
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Espeon combines inward terrain conversion with an outward anti-status layer.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High Fan-In and low exclusivity.
antiPatterns: Using Magic Bounce utility without a matchup reason

profiles.name: Excadrill
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Its Sand conversion is elite, but Sand dependence raises exclusivity compared with high-autonomy connectors.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Strong converter with meaningful Fan-In from Tailwind as well as Sand, which prevents total engine dependence.
antiPatterns: Treating Excadrill as dead whenever Sand is not active

profiles.name: Mega Excadrill
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Mega conversion can reduce the normal Sand-tax problem by making Excadrill itself a more autonomous source of pressure.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High inward conversion and better ECC than base Excadrill, though exact value depends strongly on ability/set.
antiPatterns: Spending both a weather slot and Mega slot when one of those commitments is not generating extra package value
profiles.caveat: Specific Mega Excadrill role should be revisited against current tournament sets as the M-C field settles.

profiles.name: Falinks
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Falinks has broad setup Fan-In but asks teammates to become servants more often than elite scalers do.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High convert Fan-Out, high exclusivity tax.
antiPatterns: Turning four teammates into setup insurance

profiles.name: Mega Falinks
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: The inward graph is broad, but the support tax can become extreme because Falinks itself creates little for unrelated packages.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High conversion Fan-Out paired with one of the higher exclusivity taxes in the batch.
antiPatterns: Turning four teammates into setup insurance for Falinks

profiles.name: Farfetch'd
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Farfetch'd can consume standard tempo resources but contributes little unique architecture.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Limited conversion ceiling and high opportunity cost.
antiPatterns: Spending premium support resources to compensate for low baseline power
profiles.caveat: Profile is architecture-first and intentionally conservative.

profiles.name: Farigiraf
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Farigiraf becomes elite only when several teammates can spend Trick Room or Armor Tail; then one slot feeds multiple independent engines.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Personal conversion is secondary, but ECC is respectable because Farigiraf can attack inside its own speed state.
antiPatterns: Adding Farigiraf to a team where only one slow Pokémon wants Trick Room

profiles.name: Feraligatr
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Feraligatr can consume weather or generic setup access without requiring both.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High Fan-In with moderate support tax.
antiPatterns: Making Rain exist only for Feraligatr

profiles.name: Mega Feraligatr
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Can consume both weather and generic setup infrastructure, keeping it from being a one-engine Mega.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Broad Fan-In with moderate support tax; strongest when Rain also benefits other teammates.
antiPatterns: Building Rain solely to amplify Feraligatr

profiles.name: Flamigo
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Flamigo can transform another scaler's infrastructure into a second win condition without recreating the setup process.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Exceptional shared-state conversion when Costar has a legitimate partner.
antiPatterns: Building a one-dimensional gimmick where Costar has only one possible trigger

profiles.name: Flapple
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Flapple's strongest architectural value is creating and exploiting defense-pressure sequences.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Moderate Fan-In, low-to-moderate tax.
antiPatterns: Using it as generic Dragon coverage without exploiting its debuff pressure

profiles.name: Flareon
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Flareon has multiple inward conversion routes but little outward infrastructure.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Good Fan-In, moderate exclusivity.
antiPatterns: Using both Sun and Trick Room solely for Flareon

profiles.name: Floette Eternal
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Floette Eternal is a high-Fan-In converter even before considering Mega routes.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Elite generic support conversion with very low servant tax.
antiPatterns: Forcing setup when immediate Fairy pressure is sufficient

profiles.name: Mega Floette
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: A prime example of connector bias: its outward arrows are modest, but enormous conversion Fan-In lets many ordinary support actions become a Floette clock.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Elite conversion monster with low servant tax; it can scale or attack immediately depending how expensive the free turn is.
antiPatterns: Demanding Calm Mind every game when immediate Fairy damage already wins the position
profiles.caveat: Recent Champions tournament success supports both immediate and scaling Mega Floette identities.

profiles.name: Florges
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Florges bridges Fairy offense and special-side sustain without requiring a narrow package.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Good ECC when sustain transitions into personal scaling.
antiPatterns: Using support indefinitely without converting into a clock

profiles.name: Forretress
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Forretress creates useful long-game resources, but doubles teams need immediate conversion to justify the slower chip plan.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Low personal conversion.
antiPatterns: Treating hazard accumulation as progress without a cleaner that spends it

profiles.name: Froslass
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Froslass combines matchup control and fast utility without demanding much support.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Good Fan-In with low exclusivity.
antiPatterns: Using disruption without a conversion partner

profiles.name: Mega Froslass
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Its value is often spread across disruption and matchup control rather than one visible damage engine.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Moderate-to-high Fan-In because speed and free turns can become either control or attacks.
antiPatterns: Using the Mega slot for disruption that a non-Mega could supply without opening new packages

profiles.name: Furfrou
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Furfrou's niche is damage suppression, but its limited conversion ceiling keeps MAG modest.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Low Fan-In and modest ECC.
antiPatterns: Using defensive utility without a partner that turns safety into progress

profiles.name: Gallade
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Gallade can consume opposite speed states and terrain without being dependent on any one of them.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High Fan-In with low support tax.
antiPatterns: Over-supporting setup when immediate coverage already converts

profiles.name: Mega Gallade
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: A flexible infrastructure consumer whose servant tax stays reasonable because it can usually attack without setup.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Strong Fan-In, moderate bridge quality; better as one converter among several than as the sole team centerpiece.
antiPatterns: Building excessive redirection and setup support around Gallade

profiles.name: Garbodor
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Garbodor is best when Poison control and chip feed another clock instead of being the whole win condition.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Moderate ECC and Fan-In.
antiPatterns: Relying on slow chip as the only progress engine

profiles.name: Garchomp
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Low exclusivity and broad package compatibility make base Garchomp more architecturally valuable than a simple physical-breaker label suggests.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Can spend speed control, weather, Fake Out, redirection, or simple chip without needing any one resource.
antiPatterns: Treating Garchomp as requiring Sand or dedicated setup support

profiles.name: Mega Garchomp
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Its raw conversion is excellent, but compared with base Garchomp it can impose a greater speed and Mega-slot tax.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High Fan-In and powerful conversion; strongest when Sand or Tailwind already benefits other teammates.
antiPatterns: Adding Sand and Tailwind solely to repair Mega Garchomp rather than building shared infrastructure
profiles.caveat: This row refers to the standard Mega Garchomp slug, not Mega Garchomp Z.

profiles.name: Mega Garchomp Z
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: It is easy to misclassify through old physical-Garchomp assumptions; its architectural value is closer to a fast special coverage converter.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Elite Fan-In from generic tempo resources with low servant tax and unusually broad coverage conversion.
antiPatterns: Building Sand around it automatically
Treating it as interchangeable with standard Mega Garchomp
profiles.caveat: Mega Garchomp Z is newly legal in M-C, so exact package norms are still developing. ([Champions News][1])

profiles.name: Gardevoir
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Its biggest architectural strength is not Fairy damage but the ability to bridge fast and slow packages through Trick Room without becoming passive.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Can personally spend the Trick Room it creates and still convert ordinary tempo resources.
antiPatterns: Treating Gardevoir as only a Fairy attacker

profiles.name: Mega Gardevoir
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: A premier example of engine-converter continuity: it can establish the alternate speed state and immediately become one of that state's strongest consumers.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Elite on both create and convert axes; particularly valuable in teams where Trick Room is one branch rather than the whole identity.
antiPatterns: Building a hard Trick Room six when Mega Gardevoir already supports mixed-speed architecture

profiles.name: Garganacl
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Garganacl creates its own clock and then uses durability infrastructure to extend that clock.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Elite ECC for a defensive species.
antiPatterns: Playing too passively after Salt Cure has already forced the opponent to act

profiles.name: Gengar
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Gengar's strength is that fast control and fast damage occupy the same slot.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High ECC and low exclusivity.
antiPatterns: Using Gengar as only a frail attacker

profiles.name: Mega Gengar
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Its value is not just speed and damage; fast disruption can manufacture the same free turns that Gengar itself later converts.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Excellent ECC and low exclusivity make it unusually efficient for a disruptive Mega.
antiPatterns: Using Mega Gengar as a generic fast attacker and ignoring its control leverage
profiles.caveat: Current M-C Mega results support Mega Gengar as one of the stronger-performing Mega options. ([Pokémon Zone - Pokémon TCG Pocket][2])

profiles.name: Gholdengo
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: One of the format's purest high-Fan-In converters: almost every form of tempo can become either Nasty Plot or immediate spread pressure.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Extremely low exclusivity because its preferred infrastructure is generic and usually benefits other teammates too.
antiPatterns: Greeding Nasty Plot when immediate Make It Rain already converts the board

profiles.name: Glaceon
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Glaceon can convert Snow or Trick Room strongly but creates little architecture itself.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Good inward value, moderate exclusivity.
antiPatterns: Building both Snow and Trick Room solely for Glaceon

profiles.name: Glalie
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Glalie offers mixed utility but rarely dominates either the create or conversion axis.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Moderate ECC and Fan-In.
antiPatterns: Using it without a clear role beyond Ice coverage

profiles.name: Mega Glalie
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Its damage can convert common speed and tempo resources, but the Mega slot often has to justify relatively limited outward infrastructure.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Moderate Fan-In, modest bridge value.
antiPatterns: Using several support slots merely to keep Glalie attacking

profiles.name: Glimmora
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Glimmora is unusually complete because opponent contact can create resources that its own special pressure later converts.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Elite Fan-In with near-zero servant tax.
antiPatterns: Treating chip infrastructure as sufficient without a converter

profiles.name: Mega Glimmora
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Mega Glimmora is valuable when chip creation and immediate special offense coexist rather than when either is treated as its only job.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Good ECC because chip it helps establish can later become its own cleanup resource.
antiPatterns: Building passive hazard-style pressure without immediate doubles conversion
profiles.caveat: Mega Glimmora is currently among the more successful M-C Mega options, but exact architecture depends heavily on set. ([Pokémon Zone - Pokémon TCG Pocket][2])

profiles.name: Gliscor
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Gliscor is a premium bridge because dual immunities, Ground pressure, and self-sustain create positional value across unrelated packages.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Excellent ECC through self-generated sustain.
antiPatterns: Using Gliscor only as a passive wall

profiles.name: Gogoat
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Gogoat has respectable ECC in Terrain-centered balance but limited broader reach.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Good Terrain and sustain Fan-In.
antiPatterns: Adding Terrain only to make Gogoat viable

profiles.name: Golisopod
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Its strongest architecture is usually as one of several slow or priority converters rather than a sole centerpiece.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Broad inward graph across Trick Room, Rain, Fake Out, and chip.
antiPatterns: Making every support slot serve Golisopod setup

profiles.name: Mega Golisopod
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Mega Golisopod improves dramatically when treated as one of several consumers of shared slow-game infrastructure rather than as a team that must be served.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Elite conversion Fan-In; Fake Out, Trick Room, Rain, Intimidate, and Armor Tail-style protection can all become Golisopod progress.
antiPatterns: Using Trick Room only for Golisopod
Trying to win through neutral chip instead of decisive setup conversion
profiles.caveat: Mega Golisopod is newly legal in M-C and has Tough Claws. ([Champions News][1])

profiles.name: Golurk
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Golurk is a powerful slow converter with limited engine creation.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Good Fan-In, moderate-to-high exclusivity.
antiPatterns: Creating hard Trick Room for one attacker

profiles.name: Mega Golurk
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Its coverage can be excellent under Trick Room, but speed-state dependence creates a substantial exclusivity tax.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Good slow-board converter, weak outward graph.
antiPatterns: Building hard Trick Room when only Golurk truly needs it

profiles.name: Goodra
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Goodra can inhabit several speed and defensive states without requiring any one engine.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High Fan-In with low support tax.
antiPatterns: Treating special bulk as the entire role

profiles.name: Hisuian Goodra
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Hisuian Goodra combines exceptional defensive role compression with enough offense to convert the turns it creates.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Elite defensive ECC and broad Fan-In.
antiPatterns: Using its bulk passively instead of turning survival into setup or damage

profiles.name: Gourgeist Average
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Average Gourgeist is a flexible middle-ground support form that can bridge disruption and slow-mode infrastructure.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Moderate ECC and low tax.
antiPatterns: Using Trick Room when the team has no meaningful slow converters

profiles.name: Gourgeist Large
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Large Gourgeist trades some speed for a better slow-control profile.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Moderate slow-state Fan-In.
antiPatterns: Using bulk without a partner clock

profiles.name: Gourgeist Small
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Small Gourgeist emphasizes faster support sequencing and lower exclusivity over raw bulk.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Moderate ECC with low servant tax.
antiPatterns: Using it when the extra speed does not change action order meaningfully

profiles.name: Gourgeist Super
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Super Gourgeist has the strongest slow-control conversion profile of its forms.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Good ECC when Trick Room and burn support are shared resources.
antiPatterns: Using it as pure passive bulk

profiles.name: Grafaiai
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Grafaiai's unusual utility can create entirely new interaction loops instead of merely improving an existing attacker.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Moderate personal conversion but elite create Fan-Out.
antiPatterns: Using novelty interactions without a concrete package payoff

profiles.name: Grapploct
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Grapploct is most interesting as anti-scaling control rather than raw Fighting damage.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Good opponent-state conversion, moderate support tax.
antiPatterns: Bringing it when the opponent has no scaling state worth resetting

profiles.name: Greninja
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Greninja is a premium low-tax converter because broad coverage lets it slot into many engines without becoming dependent on one.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Elite Fan-In and strong module elasticity.
antiPatterns: Over-supporting a naturally autonomous attacker

profiles.name: Mega Greninja
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Low support tax and broad coverage make it a strong example of a converter that can enter many packages without owning them.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High Fan-In from weather, speed, tempo, and simple chip.
antiPatterns: Building excessive support for a Mega that should function with light infrastructure

profiles.name: Grimmsnarl
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: An elite outward-graph species: almost any scaler can spend what Grimmsnarl creates.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Low personal conversion is acceptable because the support has extreme Fan-Out and near-zero exclusivity.
antiPatterns: Pairing screens with a six that has no durable or setup converters

profiles.name: Gyarados
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Gyarados is more than a Dragon Dance consumer because Intimidate lets it create setup access for itself and partners.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Strong ECC with excellent generic Fan-In.
antiPatterns: Using Intimidate only defensively instead of converting the reduced-pressure turn

profiles.name: Mega Gyarados
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Pre-Mega Intimidate gives the Mega form unusually strong phase-transition value rather than making the Mega merely a stat upgrade.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High ECC: it can create a safer board before Mega and then become the main converter.
antiPatterns: Mega evolving immediately when pre-Mega Intimidate or typing still has work to do

profiles.name: Hatterene
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Hatterene is an elite engine-converter because it establishes the slow state and immediately becomes one of its best consumers.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Elite ECC and Fan-In with low exclusivity if Trick Room has multiple spenders.
antiPatterns: Building hard Trick Room when Hatterene could be one mixed-speed branch

profiles.name: Hawlucha
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: A strong inward-conversion species whose best sets can reduce exclusivity by self-triggering Unburden.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Self-activation raises ECC substantially relative to terrain-only Hawlucha.
antiPatterns: Using a dedicated terrain setter only to activate Hawlucha

profiles.name: Mega Hawlucha
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Mega Hawlucha's main architecture is conversion rather than support; it needs little more than generic tempo if its base speed already fits the matchup.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Very high Fan-In but less engine creation than base Unburden identities.
antiPatterns: Over-supporting a Mega whose job should be immediate conversion

profiles.name: Heliolisk
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Heliolisk's weather-flexible abilities let it join multiple modules rather than one dedicated weather shell.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High Fan-In across weather and speed states.
antiPatterns: Choosing weather synergy that only benefits Heliolisk

profiles.name: Heracross
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Base Heracross has better ECC than its Mega when Guts lets hostile status become immediate infrastructure.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High Fan-In with manageable support tax.
antiPatterns: Over-supporting it when status or speed control already creates enough conversion

profiles.name: Mega Heracross
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: It converts many resources brilliantly, but most arrows point inward and teammates often pay heavily to manufacture its attacking turns.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Textbook high-Fan-In, high-exclusivity converter.
antiPatterns: Turning four teammates into dedicated speed, redirection, and survival support

profiles.name: Hippowdon
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Hippowdon is a durable Sand root with lower offensive conversion than Tyranitar but stronger long-game weather persistence.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Moderate ECC and high outward Fan-Out.
antiPatterns: Using Sand with no meaningful secondary consumer

profiles.name: Houndoom
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Houndoom has broad generic Fan-In and does not need a dedicated Sun shell to function.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High conversion breadth with low-to-moderate tax.
antiPatterns: Building full Sun solely for Houndoom

profiles.name: Mega Houndoom
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Sun improves it substantially, but it can still convert generic speed and tempo without making the whole team Sun-dependent.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High convert Fan-Out with moderate outward graph.
antiPatterns: Building a full Sun composition solely to enable Houndoom

profiles.name: Houndstone
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Houndstone's architecture is almost entirely inward but uniquely turns ordinary attrition into its endgame resource.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Elite late-game Fan-In, modest create-web.
antiPatterns: Sacrificing teammates unnecessarily just to increase Last Respects

profiles.name: Hydrapple
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Hydrapple can be an unusual engine hub because accuracy support benefits both itself and control partners such as sleep users.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Excellent ECC with meaningful shared-resource Fan-Out.
antiPatterns: Ignoring accuracy-support network value and treating it as only a bulky Dragon

profiles.name: Hydreigon
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Hydreigon has exceptional package flexibility because typing, Ground immunity, and speed-state adaptability let it bridge unrelated modules.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Elite Fan-In and low exclusivity.
antiPatterns: Assuming Choice Scarf or one fixed set defines the species

profiles.name: Incineroar
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: One of the format's purest engine hubs because the same Intimidate, Fake Out, and pivot package can feed almost any converter.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Personal damage is secondary, but Incineroar has strong ECC because it can repeatedly convert its own disruption into better positioning.
antiPatterns: Cycling Incineroar without a specific resource purchase

profiles.name: Indeedee Female
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Indeedee-F creates multiple distinct resources at once, so the same slot can support terrain offense, Seed activation, Trick Room, and generic setup.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Moderate personal Fan-In, but elite create Fan-Out makes low ECC irrelevant.
antiPatterns: Using Psychic Terrain when only one teammate benefits from it

profiles.name: Indeedee Male
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Male Indeedee sacrifices redirection but gains more direct engine-converter continuity through offensive and speed-state sets.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Higher personal conversion than Indeedee-F while preserving much of the same terrain Fan-Out.
antiPatterns: Copying Indeedee-F's job description instead of exploiting Male Indeedee's offensive and speed-state flexibility

profiles.name: Infernape
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Infernape has rare connector-converter overlap: Fake Out and disruption help the team, while high-speed mixed offense prevents support from becoming dead weight.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High ECC and low servant tax.
antiPatterns: Treating Infernape as only an attacker or only Fake Out support

profiles.name: Inteleon
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Inteleon is a pure high-Fan-In converter whose natural speed minimizes support tax.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High conversion breadth, low create Fan-Out.
antiPatterns: Using several support slots to enable a naturally fast attacker

profiles.name: Jolteon
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Jolteon's natural speed and immunity interaction create a low-tax converter with good positional value.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High ECC through opponent Electric targeting and pivoting.
antiPatterns: Adding redundant speed support instead of coverage or positioning

profiles.name: Kangaskhan
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Even without Mega evolution, Kangaskhan has premium low-tax tempo creation.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Good ECC and high Fan-Out.
antiPatterns: Using Fake Out without a resource purchase

profiles.name: Mega Kangaskhan
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Kangaskhan is unusual because one of its primary infrastructure moves, Fake Out, shares a slot with a fully autonomous physical converter.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Excellent ECC and low servant tax.

profiles.name: Kilowattrel

profiles.name: Klefki

antiPatterns: Using screens with no durable or setup consumers

profiles.name: Krookodile

profiles.name: Leafeon

profiles.name: Luxray

profiles.name: Maushold

profiles.name: Medicham

profiles.caveat: Form-specific Mega roles remain less tournament-established than top M-C Megas.
